title: How Pac-Man got his name
hook: Pac-Man was named after a Japanese sound for eating, and nearly something else.
peek: Pac-Man's name comes from paku paku, a Japanese word for the sound of a mouth opening and closing. In Japan he launched as Puck Man, a name that was changed before the game reached American arcades.
lede: Toru Iwatani designed Pac-Man at Namco, and it reached Japanese arcades in 1980. The name comes from paku paku, a Japanese expression for chomping, opening and closing your mouth as you eat. In Japan the game was released as Puck Man. For the American release the name became Pac-Man, reportedly to stop vandals from scratching the P into an F.

bullets.text: Iwatani has said the shape came partly from a pizza with one slice missing, and partly from simplifying the Japanese character for mouth. The pizza half is the version most often retold.
The four ghosts each follow different rules. One chases directly, others aim ahead of Pac-Man or wander, so their combined movement feels more clever than any one of them.
Iwatani wanted a game that would appeal to people who found shooting games off-putting, including women. Eating, not fighting, became the core idea.
A counting glitch breaks the 256th level: half the screen fills with jumbled symbols and the level cannot be finished. Reaching it with a perfect score was first done in 1999.
Pac-Man's name was reshaped on its way to a new market. OK started as a joke abbreviation in 1830s Boston and went on to become one of the most widely used words on Earth.
A few years later Tetris made the same leap from a single screen to the whole world, though it came from a Moscow research lab rather than a game company.
